content: Polypropylene glycol, also known as polypropylene oxide, is a polymer derived from propylene glycol. Chemically, it belongs to the polyether family. The term polypropylene glycol (PPG) is specifically used to describe polymers with low to medium molar mass, where the chemical nature of the end-groups, typically hydroxyl groups, remains significant. In contrast, the term polypropylene oxide is applied to high molar mass polymers, where the end-groups no longer have a notable impact on the polymer's properties. As of 2003, approximately 60% of the global annual production of propylene oxide, which amounted to 6.6 million tonnes, was converted into this polymer. Polypropylene glycol is synthesized through an anionic ring-opening polymerization process involving propylene oxide. The reaction requires an alcohol as the initiator and a base, commonly potassium hydroxide, as the catalyst. When ethylene glycol or water is used as the initiator, the resulting polymer has a linear structure. However, when multifunctional initiators such as glycerine, pentaerythritol, or sorbitol are employed, the polymer adopts a branched configuration. Conventional polymerization of propylene oxide typically yields an atactic polymer. An isotactic polymer can be produced using optically active propylene oxide, but this process is associated with high costs. Recent advancements have demonstrated that a salen cobalt catalyst can facilitate isotactic polymerization of racemic propylene oxide. Polypropylene glycol shares several properties with polyethylene glycol. At room temperature, it exists as a liquid. Its solubility in water decreases significantly as the molar mass increases. Additionally, the secondary hydroxyl groups present in polypropylene glycol are less reactive compared to the primary hydroxyl groups found in polyethylene glycol. Polypropylene glycol has a wide range of applications, particularly in the production of polyurethanes, where it is a key component in various formulations. It is also utilized as a rheology modifier in different industrial and commercial applications.
